text: 1775. Paul Revere rides. "The British are coming!"
Nope. He never shouted that.
Paul Revere: the midnight ride myth.
The ride was a secret mission.
British patrols were everywhere.
Shouting would get him caught.
Also, everyone there was British.
So yelling "the British" made no sense.
He reportedly said: "The Regulars are coming out."
Regulars meant British soldiers.
And he wasn't alone.
William Dawes rode too.
Revere got captured on the way to Concord.
A third rider, Samuel Prescott, made it.
So why is Revere the famous one?
A poem. 1861.
The poet Longfellow made Revere the hero.
The other two riders? Left out.
Times he shouted "The British are coming": zero.
Anyway, here's Paul Revere shouting.
